title: History of Present Illness (OPQRST)
description: Structured history of the chief complaint using the standard clinical OPQRST framework: Onset, Provocation/Palliation, Quality, Radiation, Severity, Timing. Used to characterize any acute symptom or reason for visit.

sections.title: Chief complaint
sections.instructions: Tell us about the main reason you are seeking care today.

questions.text: What is the main reason you are seeking care today?
questions.conversational_hint: To get started, can you tell me in your own words what brought you in today?

sections.title: Onset
sections.instructions: When did the problem begin and how did it start?

questions.conversational_hint: When did you first notice this — was it today, a few days ago, or has it been going on longer?

questions.text: Did this problem come on suddenly or gradually?
questions.conversational_hint: Did it come on all of a sudden, or did it develop slowly over time?

sections.title: Provocation and palliation
sections.instructions: What makes it better or worse?

questions.text: Is there anything that makes the problem worse?
questions.conversational_hint: Is there anything that seems to make it worse — like certain movements, activities, foods, or times of day?

questions.text: Is there anything that makes the problem better or gives you relief?
questions.conversational_hint: Has anything helped at all — like rest, medication, ice, heat, or a change in position?

sections.title: Quality
sections.instructions: Describe the character or quality of the symptom.

questions.text: How would you describe what the problem feels like?
questions.conversational_hint: If it's a pain or discomfort, how would you describe what it feels like — sharp, dull, burning, pressure, aching, cramping, or something else?

sections.title: Radiation
sections.instructions: Does the problem stay in one place or spread?

questions.text: Does the problem stay in one location or does it move or spread anywhere?
questions.conversational_hint: Does it stay in one spot, or does it travel or radiate to another part of your body?

sections.title: Severity
sections.instructions: How bad is the problem right now?

questions.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how severe is this problem right now? (0 = no problem, 10 = worst imaginable)
questions.conversational_hint: On a scale of 0 to 10, with 0 being no problem at all and 10 being the worst you can imagine, where would you rate this right now?

questions.text: How does this compare to when it first started — better, worse, or about the same?
questions.conversational_hint: Compared to when it first started, would you say it's getting better, getting worse, or staying about the same?

sections.title: Timing
sections.instructions: When does the problem occur and how long does it last?

questions.text: Is this problem constant, or does it come and go?
questions.conversational_hint: Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?

questions.text: When it is present, how long does an episode typically last?
questions.conversational_hint: When it does come on, how long does it tend to last — seconds, minutes, hours?

sections.title: Associated symptoms and red flags
sections.instructions: Are there any other symptoms accompanying this problem?

questions.text: Are you experiencing any of the following alongside your main complaint?
questions.conversational_hint: Along with what you described, are you also experiencing any of the following?

options.label: Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing

questions.text: Is there anything else about your symptoms you think is important for the clinician to know?
questions.conversational_hint: Is there anything else you'd like to share about what you're experiencing that you think the clinician should know?
